title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: divided-power (PD) de Rham complex, characteristic p. c_{a,b} = (a+b)!/(a! b!) is the structure constant of the divided power algebra: x^{[a]} x^{[b]} = c_{a,b} x^{[a+b]}. On the previous page Grothendieck proves that if one coefficient ξ_k (k ≥ N) of some element vanishes, then all do. He uses relations of the form c_{ℓ,k} ξ_k = c_{ℓ,k-i} ξ_{k+ℓ} and needs an ℓ for which suitable binomial coefficients are prime to p. This page isolates the combinatorial input.

Lemma 2: for all i, j ≥ 0 there exists ℓ ≥ 0 such that C(i+j+ℓ, ℓ) = c_{i+j,ℓ} and C(i+j+ℓ, i) = c_{i,j+ℓ} are both nonzero mod p. (The opening line writes c_{ℓ,i+j} and c_{ℓ+j,i}; by symmetry of c these are the same pair.)

First proof attempt on this page:
- Write i and j in base p with r+1 digits.
- Run schoolbook addition with carries ρ_α ∈ {0,1}: i_α + j_α + ρ_{α-1} = σ_α + pρ_α, with ρ_{-1} = 0 and σ_{r+1} = ρ_r.
- Define ℓ digitwise by ℓ_α = (p-1) - σ_α, so σ + ℓ = p^{r+2} - 1.
- Rewrite the carry equations as (i_α + j_α + ℓ_α) + ρ_{α-1} = (p-1) + pρ_α, plus the top-digit case.
- The sentence 'ce qui montre que l'addition des…' breaks off.

On the next page this route is abandoned for a shorter one: take ℓ = p^r - 1 - (i+j) with p^r > i+j. Then (i+j) + ℓ = i + (j+ℓ) = p^r - 1, whose base-p digits are all p-1. The 'usual criterion' (Kummer/Lucas) then says: if μ + ν = p^r - 1, then c_{μ,ν} is nonzero mod p, because no carries can occur. This gives both non-vanishings.
errors: The digitwise construction on this page is unfinished (the final sentence is cut off) and is superseded on the next page by the simpler choice ℓ = p^r - 1 - (i+j). Both choices are the same kind of ℓ: the page's ℓ is p^{r+2} - 1 - (i+j), with exponent r+2.
In (b') the parenthetical bounds the carries ρ by 0 ≤ ρ ≤ p-1. This is true but loose: the carries are 0 or 1, as he says earlier on the page.

ideas.what: Existence of ℓ making c_{i+j,ℓ} and c_{i,j+ℓ} both prime to p, by completing i+j to p^r - 1
ideas.modern_name: Kummer's theorem / Lucas's theorem on binomial coefficients mod p (no carries in base-p addition)
ideas.where_published: Standard combinatorial lemma; Berthelot's work on crystalline cohomology and divided powers uses similar arguments

ideas.what: Structure constants c_{a,b} of the divided power algebra used to show a vanishing propagates along the coefficients ξ_k
ideas.modern_name: Divided power polynomial algebra Γ(x) in characteristic p; ideals/submodules stable under the PD structure
ideas.where_published: Background to the 1976 IHÉS lecture; no published text by Grothendieck on this known to me

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary binomial-coefficient-mod-p lemma, proved by Kummer/Lucas digit arguments. It is a routine auxiliary step with nothing new for specialists.
